newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary IBUSZ 96 shr rise unfair-watchdog.
newsitem.headline: Hungary IBUSZ 96 shr rise unfair-watchdog.

text.p: Companies linked to Hungary's IBUSZ group used unfair means to push up IBUSZ share price last year but cannot be fined as the relevant law was not then in effect, the bourse watchdog said on Monday.

In the second half of December IBUSZ price soared, leading to the suspension of trading several times. This followed a decline to 600 forints earlier in the month after the stocks were bought at 900 forints in October by IBUSZ Aktiv Rt owned indirectly by IBUSZ.

"In the period investigated, no information was published which could influence the price of the shares (so) substantially," securities market watchdog APTF said in a statement in its official gazette.
Following the December fall, a purchase by Goldprint Kft, another company with IBUSZ connections, pushed the share back up to 990 forints.

Another IBUSZ-linked firm, insurance company Atlasz Biztosito Rt, then bought more stocks, pushing the price further up to 1,200 forints, while IBUSZ Aktiv sold IBUSZ shares at the same price, APTF said.
Directors of IBUSZ hold leading offices in all the above companies and the deals went through the brokerage Elso-Magyar Angol Rt, owned by IBUSZ group, APTF added.

The watchdog added that according to the laws in effect at the time of the deals, it could not fine the companies involved, but Hungary's new Securities Law which took effect in January 1 this year will enable it to do so if such cases arise in the future.
IBUSZ stood at 750 forints, down 30 at 1038 GMT.
